title: A control flow graph with loops
hints: Build the blocks exactly as in the practice; everything else is a graph question. Reachability is a depth-first walk over successors from the first block, keeping a set of blocks already seen.

For a back edge `from -> header`, the loop body is found by walking **backwards**: start at `from`, add its predecessors, their predecessors, and so on, but never go past the header (put the header in the body first, so the walk stops there). Merge bodies that share a header.
requirements: Blocks and edges are built correctly, including tail calls and calls.
Reachability starts from the first block only.
Back edges and loop bodies match the definitions, including nested loops and loops with several back edges.
Every query works on an empty function.
stretch: Print the graph in Graphviz's DOT format (`digraph { "0x0" -> "0x2"; ... }`), highlighting back edges in another colour, and view a function's structure as a picture.
